messages:
kai: heads-up: after shipping py-sdk v0.17 default batching change, console per-route latency percentiles look skewed for some tenants.

reena: oh no. default change meaning..?

kai: we lowered max_batch_wait from 20ms -> 5ms to favor latency. unintended side-effect: smaller batches => higher per-token tail latency and increased request churn in metrics. some routing policies that prefer throughput are now getting noisy.

otto: do we have a repro or logs?

kai: repro: run sdk with RDWD_MAX_BATCH_WAIT=5 and compare token throughput. curl traces show more small requests hitting route X and dropping observed throughput.

pat: is this billing-impacting or just console/SLAs?

kai: billing unaffected (post-aggregation dedupe) but console shows per-route p95 up by ~30% and token/hr graphs are fragmented leading to false alerts.

reena: which tenants affected? looks like those pinned to dedicated pools with high qps.

otto: client change should've been opt-in. Did release notes/nudges mention default flip?

kai: default flip was in release notes but only inside changelog; not surfaced in console or deprecation banner. my mistake.

pat: quick mitigation options: 1) revert default in SDK patch, 2) server-side routing policy that smooths p95 by reaggregating small batches, 3) console flag to show "batching-adjusted" metrics.

reena: revert seems simplest and fastest. we can ship py-sdk 0.17.1 with old default and patch docs. do we also need TS/Go parity?

otto: TS already on 2.x with old default; Go not changed. we should coordinate parity but revert first.

ci-bot: ci/tests: py-sdk unit -> failing on batch-timer-tests (1835010100) :x:

pat: tests failing because some test expects 5ms behavior. update tests or use feature-flag. but revert release should cut immediate noise.

kai: opened py-sdk#1300 revert PR (set RDWD_MAX_BATCH_WAIT default back to 20ms). adding a config env RDWD_BATCH_FALLBACK=legacy so we can flip later.

reena: server-side, can we add a short-term routing policy mapping that treats many small requests within 10ms window as a single logical batch for metrics? basically dedupe for console only.

otto: that sounds doable: ingest can coalesce events with close timestamps and same tenant+route. low-risk because it's metrics-only. I'll open ingest PR and gate it behind a feature flag.

pat: console change: add "batch-corrected" view toggle on latency tile and a banner noting it's for migration. owners? reena(console), otto(ingest), kai(sdk).

deploy-bot: deploy ingest-canary v4.12.0-rc -> started (1835010200)

ci-bot: py-sdk#1300 tests -> updated (1835010220) :white_check_mark: 

otto: ingest canary rolled to 5% tenants. monitoring p95 delta.

reena: added console toggle metrics.batch_corrected, tooltip explains why numbers differ. also added docs blurb and changelog entry.

kai: merged py-sdk#1300 and cut py-sdk v0.17.1 -> publish queued.

deploy-bot: ingest-canary v4.12.0-rc -> success (1835010250) :white_check_mark:

pat: early signals: p95 normalizing on flagged tenants. alerts quieting.

otto: follow-ups: 1) schedule cross-SDK audit for defaults (kai), 2) add explicit migration notes and runtime flag in console (reena), 3) add long-term eval to see if lower wait helps throughput at scale (otto).

kai: TL;DR: accidental default change in py-sdk reduced batch wait -> more small requests -> console p95 spikes. short-term: revert SDK default + ingest dedupe + console toggle. mid-term: deliberate rollout plan + metrics impact eval.

reena: thanks all. I'll post a short customer-facing note for tenants who saw alerts. recon in 2 hours to recheck dashboards. :white_check_mark:
